matchups.name: instant reanimator
matchups.stance_rationale: Sanctifier en-Vec and Thraben Charm both attack the graveyard the whole deck is built on, and Orim's Chant buys the exact turn Martyr of Sands needs; none of the three costs our own plan anything.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: counters a triggered ability for one mana, against a deck that is almost nothing else: Solitude, Flickerwisp, Starfield Shepherd, Overlord of the Balemurk and the Abiding Grace end-step return are all triggers, and all five stay in on this row. Three or four copies in ten of ten recorded boards, and it was missing from this row entirely.

each opponent can cast spells only when they could cast a sorcery, which turns off Thraben Charm on their combo turn, Orim's Chant on their upkeep and Ephemerate in response to removal. Nine of ten recorded boards.

X sweeper: at X=1 it takes eight of our post-board cards - four Serra Ascendant and four Martyr of Sands, because Kami of False Hope and Thraben Inspector are both on this row's out list - against a Nihil Spellbomb of their own if one is on the battlefield, and nothing else of theirs.
one mana, no colour requirement, exiles our graveyard at instant speed: Abiding Grace and Emeria, the Sky Ruin then have nothing to return. Six of ten boards.

instant-speed X exile that answers a resolved Sanctifier en-Vec through its protection - it is white, so protection from black and red does not see it. One or two copies maindeck in seven of ten lists as well as boarded in five of ten, so it is a game-one answer too.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Goryo's Vengeance returns Atraxa on turn two or three, and a 7/7 flier kills through 30 life faster than Martyr of Sands can rebuild it.

key_cards.why: instant-speed two-mana reanimation, which is what makes the kill turn two or three rather than turn seven.
the payoff body: its enters trigger refuels them on the same turn the clock starts, so racing it is not an option.
three or four copies maindeck in ten of ten recorded lists, not the sideboard one-of the row used to name: it answers a resolved Sanctifier en-Vec in game one and costs them no mana to do it.
rebuys the Atraxa trigger and dodges our Solitude, so one answer does not stop the fast draw.

survives_opposing_board.why: an instant that exiles their graveyard in response to Goryo's Vengeance targeting; it is never a permanent, so March of Otherworldly Light cannot answer it.

its replacement effect exiles Atraxa instead of letting it reach the graveyard, so Goryo's Vengeance has no target; the protection from black is not what does that, since Goryo's targets their own graveyard. It is not close to a lock, though, because their answers are white and maindeck: one or two Prismatic Ending in ten of ten lists exile it at two colours for mana value 2, three or four Solitude in ten of ten exile it for free on the turn it lands, and one or two March of Otherworldly Light sit in seven of ten maindecks and five of ten boards. Three or four Thoughtseize in ten of ten take it from hand before any of that. Deploy it into their tapped-out turn and expect to need the second copy.

one mana at instant speed on their combo turn, and it is not uncontested: Force of Negation is a maindeck two-to-three-of in ten of ten recorded lists. Cast on their turn, which is where the Goryo's Vengeance is, the Force costs them {1}{U}{U} rather than a blue card - so the Chant is a tax they have to pay mana for, not a free answer they always have. Teferi, Time Raveler is the worse card here: exactly one copy each time - maindeck in three of the ten lists and one more in each of nine boards - and under it we cannot cast the Chant on their turn at all.

play_plan.keep: Two lands plus Thraben Charm or Orim's Chant; a hand of only lifegain loses on turn three.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Sanctifier en-Vec on two, then Martyr of Sands with four white cards in hand.
play_plan.watch_for: Two open black mana with a full graveyard is the Goryo's turn - hold the Charm.
play_plan.posture_why: we cannot race a turn-three Atraxa.

matchups.name: broodscale bloodchief
matchups.stance_rationale: High Noon and Orim's Chant attack the turn the combo happens rather than the pieces, which is what a post-board 60 whose only answer to a resolved Equipment is two Skyclave Apparition has against a two-card loop. The 75 also holds three Wrath of the Skies, which destroys Blade of the Bloodchief at mana value 1, but this row does not board them - they take our ten mana-value-1 creatures with it.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: permanent cards in graveyards cannot enter the battlefield, so Abiding Grace and Emeria, the Sky Ruin both stop returning anything, on a 0/4 body that also blocks the combat version of the kill. Nine of ten recorded boards, and it was named nowhere in this row.
the same answer for one mana on the half that matters here - creature cards in graveyards cannot enter, so the Kami of False Hope loop stops. Eight of ten boards.

eight of ten recorded boards, and the mode that matters is the first: exile target creature with power OR toughness 1 or less takes Martyr of Sands, a Serra Ascendant short of 30, Kami of False Hope, Thraben Inspector and Flickerwisp at instant speed for two mana - both Enduring Innocence are on this row's out list, so they are not part of it. The second mode counters a sorcery, which is Wrath of the Skies rather than High Noon, an enchantment, and Wrath is not boarded here.
the cast trigger exiles a noncreature nonland permanent of mana value 4 or less, which is High Noon or an Abiding Grace, and it resolves whether or not the 3/4 body does. Nine of ten boards.
one mana at instant speed on High Noon or Abiding Grace; the four life it gives us is a cost they are happy to pay against a deck that gains nine a Martyr. Ten of ten boards.

three damage to each creature with and without flying when both {R} and {G} are spent, which kills every creature in our mainboard except Overlord of the Balemurk and a Serra Ascendant past 30 life. Three of ten boards. It is symmetric here, which is why they hold it: Basking Broodscale and Glaring Fleshraker are 2/2 and die to it as well. Whipflare, at one copy in one of ten, is a different and worse card against us - two damage, and only to nonartifact creatures.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Two cards make an arbitrarily large attacker and a third turns it into direct damage, so the game is decided by whether they assemble before we can tax the turn.

key_cards.why: the half of the loop that is also a fine fair creature, so they never have to hold it back.
a one-mana Equipment that puts a +1/+1 counter on the Broodscale whenever a creature dies, and the Spawn that counter makes is the creature that dies - infinite mana and an unbounded body.
one damage to each opponent whenever ANOTHER colorless creature THEY control enters - our creatures never trigger it - which turns the loop from a combat kill into a drain no life total outruns.

survives_opposing_board.why: two Nature's Claim in ten of ten boards, a maindeck Haywire Mite in ten of ten, one or two maindeck Boseiju, Who Endures in ten of ten and two Thief of Existence in nine of ten all answer a resolved High Noon, so what it buys is the turn and the card they spend on it rather than a lock. Orim's Chant is the second copy of the same tax, and the tax is the half of the plan that holds whether the kill is combat or a Glaring Fleshraker drain.
an instant that resolves before their first spell; nothing in their board answers a spell on the stack.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and one of High Noon or Orim's Chant; a pure lifegain hand does not interact.
play_plan.goldfish_for: High Noon on turn two, then a clock while they can only cast one spell a turn.
play_plan.watch_for: Blade of the Bloodchief down with one green open is the Nature's Claim turn - lead with the second tax.
play_plan.posture_why: once Glaring Fleshraker is down the kill needs no attack step, so we tax the turn.

matchups.name: eldrazi ramp
matchups.stance_rationale: White Orchid Phantom destroys the Eldrazi Temple or Ugin's Labyrinth the whole curve is built on, and it does it on a 2/2 flier with first strike that Phelia and Ephemerate can rebuy.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: every spell costs at least three, which taxes seventeen of our mainboard cards and all three alternative costs the deck is built on: Solitude's evoke, Overlord of the Balemurk's impending and Starfield Shepherd's warp. Eight of ten recorded boards, and the hardest single card in the field against this 75.

on one it counters Serra Ascendant, Martyr of Sands, Thraben Inspector and Ephemerate - twelve cards post-board, thirteen in game one, since this row boards the Kami of False Hope out. On two it counters four Phelia and the three White Orchid Phantom this row brings in, which is the setting that actually beats the plan.

free for one green card exiled on our turn, and it destroys two enchantments at instant speed with their mana committed elsewhere. Not Abiding Grace, which this row boards out: post-board the targets are four Overlord of the Balemurk and two Enduring Innocence, both Enchantment Creatures on the type line whether or not the Overlord is impending, plus a Thraben Inspector Clue. Six of ten recorded boards carry it, at two, two, three, three, three and three copies, so four of ten cannot punish an enchantment at all - whether the second one is held back is a read on which of the ten is across the table rather than the default line.

its enters trigger puts our graveyard on the bottom of the library, and the evoke cost is a green card rather than mana, so it costs nothing on the turn it matters. This row boards Abiding Grace out, so what it takes is Emeria, the Sky Ruin's returns and Overlord of the Balemurk's - and it leaves a 3/4 reach blocker in front of the Phantom. Six of ten boards.

a 6/6 vigilance reach trample blocker whose attack-or-block trigger is modal - a 3/3 Beast, three life, or a card - so it is three life only on the turns they choose it, and the 3/3 mode is the one that outgrows a stalled board.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Their threats are individually larger than ours and replace themselves, so they win a long game unless the mana that casts them early is attacked.

key_cards.why: a 3/3 that searches out a land on cast and, kicked for {1}{C}, exiles one of ours - four copies in ten of ten lists, so the mana attack runs in both directions.

exiles one coloured permanent on cast and one more per colorless spell afterwards, so a wide board is answered one card a turn rather than swept - which is why we flood against it rather than holding back.

what Fight Rigging is digging for - Green Sun's Zenith cannot find it, since the Zenith fetches a green creature and Emrakul is colorless. Fight Rigging casts it rather than putting it onto the battlefield, so the cast trigger takes our next turn, and protection from instants means only a creature answers the 13/13 afterwards: an evoked Solitude, which hands them thirteen life.

survives_opposing_board.why: the land destruction is an enters trigger, so it is paid the moment the Phantom resolves and Chalice of the Void on two is the only card that stops it - and a Chalice on two also stops four Phelia, which is the rest of the blink half, so it is not a cheap setting for them either. The body is a different question: four maindeck Kozilek's Command in ten of ten recorded lists exile a creature of mana value X or less at instant speed, and Dismember, Unholy Heat and Blasphemous Act follow it out of the board. Cast it for the land, never for the clock.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and White Orchid Phantom, or a hand that curves out under a Chalice on one.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Phantom on their Eldrazi Temple, then blink it with Phelia for the second land.
play_plan.watch_for: A first-turn Chalice on one means the nine mana-value-1 creatures left post-board are dead cards.
play_plan.posture_why: their curve only works off the two accelerating lands.

matchups.name: dimir control
matchups.stance_rationale: White Orchid Phantom attacks a manabase that is almost entirely nonbasic, on a body that blinks - a line the maindeck does not have against a deck that answers threats one at a time.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: Sunburst, so one colour of mana spent means one charge counter and it destroys each nonland permanent of mana value exactly 1 - eight of our post-board cards on this row, since Kami of False Hope and Thraben Inspector are both on the out list, including a Serra Ascendant that has already crossed 30 life. Three mana in total. Ten of ten boards.
one mana to counter a triggered ability, which is the Abiding Grace end-step return, Emeria and every enters trigger in the deck. Nine of ten boards.

-X/-X to all creatures for X life, which is the sweeper Engineered Explosives cannot be: the Explosives destroys one mana-value band at a time, and Solitude, Skyclave Apparition, Starfield Shepherd and Overlord of the Balemurk are all above the one it is set to. Six life against a deck that gains nine a Martyr is a price they pay. Nine of ten boards.
one mana, exiles our graveyard at instant speed, and Abiding Grace and Emeria then have nothing to return. Eight of ten boards.

nonbasic lands are Islands, so eight of our thirteen nonbasics stop producing {W} - three Shadowy Backstreet, two Godless Shrine, Mistveil Plains and two Emeria - and the other five, the fetchlands, lose their fetch ability and become Islands that tap for {U}. Eight of ten boards, and Skyclave Apparition at mana value 3 is the answer.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Every card they play trades one-for-one, so the game is decided by which side still has a card advantage engine on turn eight.

key_cards.why: flash, and the ping kills Martyr of Sands, Kami of False Hope and a Serra Ascendant that has not crossed 30 life; then they amass Orcs 1.
a two-mana threat that draws cards and grows, so they never run out first.
takes the engine card out of the opening hand, which is why redundancy beats quality here.

survives_opposing_board.why: first strike beats Orcish Bowmasters and the body is above the one damage their pings deal. Fatal Push maindeck and Toxic Deluge at X=2 both answer it, and either one is a card not spent on Serra Ascendant.

play_plan.keep: Two lands, a threat and a second threat; a hand with one card that matters loses to Thoughtseize.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Resolve two threats a turn until one sticks, then Martyr of Sands out of removal range.
play_plan.watch_for: Nihil Spellbomb held up means Abiding Grace and Emeria are about to be blanked.
play_plan.posture_why: they answer threats one at a time and we have more of them.

matchups.name: ur cutter prowess
matchups.stance_rationale: Cori-Steel Cutter makes a token every turn, so removal one at a time loses; the sweeper is the only card that resets a board they rebuild for free.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: ten of ten boards - three copies in five of them - but only three of the ten play it maindeck, so it is a post-board card rather than a game-one one. One mana for six damage with delirium, and the only card in their 75 that kills a 6/6 Serra Ascendant - Lightning Bolt is three damage and Lava Dart is one. It is not rare in the wider field, where Solitude and Path to Exile exile her outright and Kozilek's Command does it at X=1, that last one because she is mana value 1 however large she has grown.

no maindeck copies anywhere and nine of ten boards, three copies in five of them. Counters mana value 2 exactly: the four Phelia maindeck, and Sanctifier en-Vec after boarding, which is the card this matchup's plan rests on and the only way their deck beats a resolved one. Skyclave Apparition and Abiding Grace are 3, and a warped Starfield Shepherd is still 5 - warp is an alternative cost, not a mana value.

ten of ten boards, four copies in five of them and three in the other five. One mana with replicate, countering a triggered ability - which is most of what this deck does: Phelia, Flickerwisp, Solitude, Skyclave Apparition, Starfield Shepherd, Overlord of the Balemurk and the Abiding Grace end step are all triggers. It does not touch Martyr of Sands, whose ability is activated rather than triggered and is not a spell.

one or two copies in nine of ten boards, one in five of them. It cannot touch Sanctifier en-Vec, which is a creature spell - but Wrath of the Skies is not, and this row rests on Wrath of the Skies. One blue mana taxes it by {2}, so the X=1 sweeper costs five mana out of a 22-land deck or it does not resolve.

one or two copies in six of ten boards, and five of ten add one or two Surgical Extraction on top. Free to cast, then tap and sacrifice to exile our graveyard, which is the fuel for Abiding Grace and Emeria, the Sky Ruin.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Cori-Steel Cutter turns their second spell each turn into a body, so their damage per turn grows while their card count does not fall.

key_cards.why: a Monk on their second spell each turn, at most one a turn, which is why one removal spell a turn never catches up.
surveil on every noncreature spell, and with delirium online a 3/3 flier that has to attack - the card that makes their one-drops a clock rather than a chump blocker.

four copies in nine of the ten maindecks. {1}{R} for a 1/2 with flying and haste that gets +2/+0 on every noncreature spell, so it is lethal out of nowhere, and at mana value 2 it lives through our own Wrath of the Skies at X=1 - and it is not the only card that does, because Cori-Steel Cutter is {1}{R} and an artifact, and Wrath destroys artifacts as well as creatures.

three or four maindeck in all ten lists and free - {G/P} is 2 life, not mana. +2/+2 wins the combat our 2/2s and 3/2s are supposed to win, and it is a noncreature spell, so it triggers prowess and Dragon's Rage Channeler surveil while it does.

survives_opposing_board.why: Spell Snare counters mana value 2 and Wrath of the Skies is {X}{W}{W}, so at any X above zero it is out of range of the Snare. Spell Pierce is the one that reaches it - one or two copies in nine of ten recorded boards, countering a noncreature spell unless we pay {2} - so the sweeper wants two more lands than the X, not none. Nothing in their board counters it outright.

protection from red blanks Unholy Heat, Lightning Bolt and every Monk token's damage, so once it resolves their whole damage suite is dead against it. The game is decided on the stack instead: one to three Spell Snare in nine of ten recorded boards counter it exactly, at mana value 2, and Into the Flood Maw in two of ten bounces a resolved one. Deploy it when they are tapped out or after a Phelia has drawn the Snare.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and a way to interact; a hand of only one-drops loses to the first sweeper or Cutter.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Sanctifier en-Vec on turn two, then Wrath of the Skies at X=1 once they commit.
play_plan.watch_for: After boarding, one open red with delirium online is Unholy Heat - six damage kills anything, including a 6/6.
play_plan.posture_why: Cori-Steel Cutter outgrows any board we build.

matchups.self_cost: Wrath of the Skies at X=1 answers their Dragon's Rage Channeler, Monastery Swiftspear and every Monk token, and takes our own mana-value-1 half with them: nine copies in this matchup rather than ten, because Kami of False Hope is one of the cards boarded out. What X=1 does not answer is either card at mana value 2: Slickshot Show-Off, and Cori-Steel Cutter, four copies in ten of ten maindecks and an Artifact - Equipment that the sweeper would destroy at X=2, so the Monks start again on their next two-spell turn. Going to X=2 is not free, because our own four Phelia at {1}{W} and both Sanctifier en-Vec at {W}{W} are mana value 2, and the Sanctifier is the card this whole row rests on - so X=1 is the setting, and the Cutter is answered by the blocker they cannot burn rather than by the sweeper. Nothing rebuilds afterwards, and that is a decision rather than an oversight - both Abiding Grace come out here too, so the sweeper has to pay for itself on the turn it resolves. It does, because everything at mana value 2 or more lives through our own X=1 - twenty-three copies post-board: four Phelia and two Sanctifier en-Vec at two; two Skyclave Apparition, three Flickerwisp and two Enduring Innocence at three; and four Solitude, four Starfield Shepherd and the two Overlord of the Balemurk that stay in, at five. Of that list the two Sanctifier en-Vec are what the plan rests on, because their whole damage suite is red and cannot touch it - the exceptions this row already records are blue bounce, which moves it rather than answering it. The other twenty-one copies are what stops them rebuilding into an empty board. Against three Unholy Heat and three or four Consign to Memory the one-for-one game is already lost; the sweeper is how a Sanctifier they cannot burn ends up the last permanent standing.

matchups.name: boros aggro
matchups.stance_rationale: The maindeck already wins this: Martyr of Sands gains more per activation than their whole curve deals per turn, so the board adds a body their removal cannot touch rather than another answer.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: at X=1 it sweeps ten of our mainboard cards and their own Ocelot Pride, Guide of Souls and Ragavan too - three four-ofs, which is why they board it rather than lead on it. Their X is a floor rather than a cap: energy is banked, and four Guide of Souls collect {E} on every creature that enters while four Galvanic Discharge hand them three at a time, so they may pay more than the X they announced. Ours is a hard cap - nothing in the 75 makes energy.
exiles our graveyard and keeps it empty, which blanks Abiding Grace and Emeria, the Sky Ruin permanently. Six of ten boards, at one, one, one, one, two and three copies.

eight of ten boards at two to four copies, three the most common and only one list on four. A 4/4 flier that destroys one of our thirteen nonbasics on arrival; it costs {1} less for each land we control that could produce {C}, and none of ours can, so it always costs the full {3}{R}{R}.
ten of ten boards, two copies in eight of them. The Tear half is one mana at instant speed for Abiding Grace, Enduring Innocence or an Overlord of the Balemurk - all three are enchantments.

nine of ten boards at one to three copies, and four of ten lists play one maindeck as well, so four of ten can show it in game one. Thirteen of our twenty-two lands become Mountains with no rules text, so Marsh Flats and Flooded Strand stop fetching and Emeria stops being an engine; nine basic Plains is why this is a tempo hit rather than a lock.

ten of ten boards, two copies in five of them and one in the other five. Whenever a player casts a spell, if no mana was spent to cast it, counter that spell - which is our evoked Solitude. It is symmetric and not quite free for them: one of the ten lists plays a single maindeck Solitude of its own, and that list boards two Vexing Bauble.

six of ten boards, two copies in each. One spell a turn is a real cost to a deck that wants Martyr of Sands and Abiding Grace in the same turn; High Noon is {1}{W} and mana value 2, so Skyclave Apparition exiles it and is our only maindeck answer.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Guide of Souls gains them life too and Goblin Bombardment turns the board into reach, so they can race a lifegain deck rather than only attack into it.

key_cards.why: a turn-one clock that also steals the card that would have answered it.
gains them a life whenever another creature enters, so Ocelot Pride's Cats and Ajani's token pay too, which is what makes the lifegain race close rather than free.
a free sacrifice outlet that turns a board of one-drops into direct damage, so blocking and Kami of False Hope both stop mattering.

two maindeck copies in ten of ten lists, and two of its three modes are pointed at us: destroy target enchantment, which is Abiding Grace, and exile any number of target players' graveyards, which is the recursion. Instant speed, game one, every list.

survives_opposing_board.why: protection from red means Galvanic Discharge, Lightning Bolt and Goblin Bombardment cannot damage it and no red creature blocks it profitably. Two maindeck Thraben Charm in ten of ten lists are the game-one answer - the damage mode is white, so protection does not see it, and twice their creature count clears two easily - and their boarded Wrath of the Skies at X=2 is the post-board one, which costs them their own board.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and Martyr of Sands, or two lands and Serra Ascendant with a white card behind it.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Turn-one Serra Ascendant, turn-two Martyr of Sands revealing four white cards for twelve, then attack for six.
play_plan.watch_for: Ranger-Captain of Eos, maindeck in all ten lists: sacrificing it is free and stops us casting noncreature spells that turn, which blanks a held Ephemerate.
play_plan.posture_why: a resolved Martyr of Sands puts us out of burn range in one activation.

matchups.name: esper blink
matchups.stance_rationale: This is the shell we adopted with a better removal suite, and the half that is ours to win is the Martyr of Sands loop their one-for-one removal cannot answer; the board adds a mana attack rather than a second engine.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: two to four copies in ten of ten recorded boards, countering a triggered ability for one mana: the Abiding Grace end-step return, Emeria, and every enters trigger in the deck. It was missing from this row while a one-of in three of ten was named.
two or three copies in nine of ten boards; one spell a turn is a tax on the deck that rebuilds a board, not on the deck that holds one flier and a removal spell.

at X=1 it sweeps the nine mana-value-1 creatures left after this row cuts the Kami of False Hope, and leaves their two- and three-drops. Ten in game one - and one of the ten recorded lists maindecks a single copy, so it is not strictly a post-board card; the other nine hold two to four in the board only.

activated abilities of artifacts, creatures and planeswalkers cannot be activated, so Martyr of Sands, Kami of False Hope and the Thraben Inspector Clue all stop; Mistveil Plains and the fetchlands are lands and keep working, and Abiding Grace and Emeria are triggered abilities it does not touch. Six of ten boards.
exiles our graveyard every turn, which is a permanent answer to Abiding Grace and Emeria, the Sky Ruin. Three of ten boards, so it is the one to expect least.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Both decks rebuy enters triggers, so the game goes long and is decided by which engine survives a sweeper rather than by the board on turn four.

key_cards.why: two to four copies in nine of ten recorded lists, and its enters trigger destroys an artifact or enchantment: Abiding Grace and Enduring Innocence are answered in game one, and Phelia or Ephemerate does it again.
a 4/6 flier for {3}{U}{U} or warped in for {1}{U}, drawing two a turn once they are low on cards - the card-advantage engine that beats us in a long game.
free removal for our Serra Ascendant, four copies in ten of ten lists, and Ephemerate rebuys it.
holds us to sorcery speed, which costs us Ephemerate as a protection spell and Solitude as an ambush.

survives_opposing_board.why: their manabase is fetches and duals behind two basic Plains and a Swamp in nine of ten lists, one Plains in the tenth, and an Island in four - so the search clause usually replaces the land and what the Phantom really costs them is the turn. Fatal Push answers the body, and that is a removal spell not spent on Serra Ascendant.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and Martyr of Sands, or two lands and a threat that survives Fatal Push.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Martyr of Sands into Abiding Grace, gaining nine a turn while they answer one threat.
play_plan.watch_for: Clarion Conqueror turns off Martyr of Sands, Kami of False Hope and the Clue - not the lands, not the recursion triggers. Solitude and Skyclave Apparition both exile it.
play_plan.posture_why: their removal is one-for-one and our engine recurs.

matchups.name: living end
matchups.stance_rationale: Thraben Charm exiles their graveyard at instant speed with the cascade trigger on the stack, and Orim's Chant stops the cascade spell being cast at all; neither costs our own plan anything.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: two or three copies in five of ten recorded boards, and it turns off Martyr of Sands and Kami of False Hope - the fog loop this row calls its backup plan - while costing their own hasteless board nothing.
three damage to each creature: everything in our mainboard except Overlord of the Balemurk and a Serra Ascendant past 30 life. Six of ten boards.

free for one green card exiled, but only on our turn - the alternative cost reads 'if it's not your turn' - and it destroys two Abiding Grace at once at instant speed. Eight of ten boards, which is more than the Leyline.
evoked for {1}{G}, and its destroy is an enters trigger rather than a held effect, so it answers a resolved Abiding Grace rather than a window.

a replacement effect that exiles our cards instead of letting them reach the graveyard, one-sidedly, so Abiding Grace and Emeria stop having targets - it does not touch what is already there, so only an opening-hand copy is a blowout. Four copies, and in two of ten boards it is the least likely of these five.

opponent_plan.posture_why: One resolved Living End makes a whole board and sweeps ours at the same time, so the game ends on their cascade turn rather than on a damage race.

key_cards.why: one card turns their cycled graveyard into a lethal board. It exiles graveyards BEFORE it sacrifices boards, so the creatures it sacrifices do not come back - what returns is what was already in the graveyard, ours included.
cascades into the payoff at instant speed for three mana, on their turn or at the end of ours.
the second cascade shell, so the payoff is effectively a six-of and one answer does not stop it.

four maindeck in ten of ten lists. Free by exiling a blue card when it is not their turn, which is exactly the window our Thraben Charm wants at our end step; {1}{U}{U} when they cascade on their own turn.

survives_opposing_board.why: Force of Vigor and Foundation Breaker cannot answer an instant that is never on the battlefield, but two maindeck four-ofs can. Endurance is four copies in ten of ten lists with flash and an evoke cost of one green card, and its enters trigger puts their own graveyard on the bottom of their library in response to the Charm. matchups.name: devoted combo

That is the answer to the question this row exists to ask: a board of mana dorks IS a Wrath target at the X it wants, and neither doubler that matters is. Leyline of Abundance is mana value 4 and survives until six mana, and Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler is a planeswalker, which the card does not name at any X. So the sweeper resets the board without answering the engine, and Skyclave Apparition and Thraben Charm's enchantment mode are what answer the engine. Thraben Charm and Orim's Chant cost us nothing, so the whole symmetry is the sweeper's. Two recorded differences separate this row from the `creatures toolbox` row of the same deck and both point the same way: Suncleanser, whose second mode takes the energy this card is our only source of, is in ONE of ten pulled boards under the live label against five of ten under the retired one, and Crystal Barricade is in ten of ten against four of ten. The sweeper is therefore both safer than that row says and more necessary, because the Barricade is what blanks the cheaper Thraben Charm damage mode.

sideboard_audit.why: The mana attack this shell does not otherwise have, on a body the rest of the deck already knows what to do with: a 2/2 first-strike flier that Phelia and Ephemerate rebuy for a second and third land. It is boarded against every recorded matchup whose lands do more than produce mana - urzatron's Urza lands, eldrazi ramp's Eldrazi Temple and Ugin's Labyrinth, amulet titan's bounce lands and Boseiju, pinnacle affinity's Urza's Saga, and the two- and three-colour manabases of dimir control, esper blink and esper control. urzatron is the only Tron deck of the seven. The compensation clause is why this is not a Stone Rain and also why it is better than one: they may search a basic and it enters tapped, so they keep a land but never that land. A basic does not assemble Tron, does not make the {C}{C} an Eldrazi Temple makes for colorless Eldrazi, is not a bounce land for an Amulet of Vigor to untap into two mana, and replaces one colour where the land it took was covering two or three. Running the basics out is the smaller half of the card and bites only where they are few - pinnacle affinity at two in eight of ten, urzatron at one or two in nine of ten, the tenth running six Islands and never running out. eldrazi ramp, amulet titan, dimir control, esper blink and esper control hold three to five, so there it is always the land taken that matters and never the search. urzatron left the field this pass; the remaining six rows still clear the versatile bar comfortably.

Two mana at instant speed for graveyard exile against the four recursion decks - cast with the cascade trigger or the Persist on the stack rather than on an empty yard - and for the enchantment mode against both halves of the one green combo deck the field records under two labels, where four Leyline of Abundance in ten of ten recorded lists are the accelerant that gets Devoted Druid and Vizier of Remedies down a turn early. It replaces the boros ponza row this pass retired at 1.72pp; the mode that row was boarded for was the same one, aimed at Rest in Peace instead. The damage mode is the third use and the reason it is not a dead draw on an empty graveyard: damage equal to twice the creatures we control kills a 0/2 Devoted Druid or a 2/1 Vizier of Remedies off a single body, though Crystal Barricade in ten of ten devoted combo boards prevents it reaching anything except the Barricade. It is never a permanent, so it is the one piece of interaction in the board that Force of Vigor, Foundation Breaker and Meltdown are all blank against. This pass drops goryos vengeance from the field and adds esper goryo in its place - the same graveyard-reanimation shell under a different label, so the card's role is unchanged.

A two-mana tax on the turn a combo deck goes off, which is the only interaction this 75 has against a kill that never touches the battlefield. It is paired with Orim's Chant in two of the three matchups it is boarded for - amulet titan is the exception and takes it alongside White Orchid Phantom instead - because each of those decks carries two to four answers to an enchantment in its recorded 75 and needs them on the turn they combo rather than a turn early. Its cumulative share FELL this pass while the field grew, and the reason is a decision rather than drift: the 19th row, devoted combo, is the one combo matchup in the field High Noon does not serve, because that kill is a single Green Sun's Zenith plus activated abilities and a loyalty ability, all of which resolve under a one-spell-per-turn tax. ruby storm left the field this pass; the remaining three rows still clear the 8.0pp versatile bar at 9.19pp.

The only card in the 75 that answers a board that has already gone wide. Every matchup it is boarded for is one where their threats are individually bigger than ours, so trading whole boards is the exchange that favours us. What makes a symmetric sweeper asymmetric is the rebuild afterwards, and that holds on one of the five rows rather than all five: boros energy keeps both halves, and even there it is not unconditional. Abiding Grace triggers at the beginning of our own end step and is modal - gain 1 life, or return a creature card with mana value 1 - so it is one creature per turn cycle at most and only on the turns we choose that mode. Emeria, the Sky Ruin returns a creature card at our upkeep only if we control seven or more Plains, which out of fifteen Plains-typed lands in twenty-two means seven of them on the battlefield rather than in the deck. ur cutter prowess boards Abiding Grace out against four Consign to Memory, and pinnacle affinity keeps it but plays into three or four maindeck Tormod's Crypt; on those two rows the sweeper is justified by what survives our own X instead, which is everything at mana value 2 or more. The two rows for the one green combo deck are where the exchange is widest, because their whole engine sits at mana value 2 or less - and the two labels disagree about the answer to it. Suncleanser, which takes the energy this card is the only source of, is five of ten boards under the retired `creatures toolbox` label and ONE of ten under the live `devoted combo` one, so the newer row is the more confident of the two. This pass adds 45c aggro, whose own domain one- and two-drops - Territorial Kavu and Scion of Draco - sit in the same mana-value band as our own creatures, so the exchange there reads the same as boros energy: a card they hold rather than lead with.

Protection from black and from red on a two-mana body, plus a replacement effect that exiles their black and red cards instead of letting them reach a graveyard. Against the two reanimator decks it is a lock on the engine rather than an answer to one copy. Against the three red aggro decks it is a blocker none of their damage can touch, which is not the same as untouchable: boros energy plays a maindeck Static Prison in ten of ten lists that exiles it, a maindeck Thraben Charm whose damage mode is white, and a boarded Wrath of the Skies that destroys it at X of two or more. Both halves earn the slot at two copies. The cost is on our side and is recorded in NOTES.md: Overlord of the Balemurk is the only black card in the 75, and with a Sanctifier out our own Overlords are exiled rather than binned. This pass drops ruby storm and goryos vengeance and adds esper goryo, the same reanimation shell, and 45c aggro, whose burn suite (Lightning Bolt, Tribal Flames) is entirely red and cannot touch it.

One mana at instant speed for a Time Walk on the turn a combo deck kills. Kept at two copies as a maintainer decision recorded on mtg-decks#48 rather than argued from the field, and it clears the versatile bar on its own: it is boarded for the six recorded combo matchups - instant reanimator, broodscale bloodchief, allosaurus combo, both labels of the one green creature-combo deck (creatures toolbox and devoted combo), and living end - a 21.67pp cumulative share, the widest in the board. The green combo rows are the ones where the Time Walk half can be turned off rather than answered: Crystal Barricade gives its controller hexproof in ten of ten lists under the live creatures toolbox label, and the card then has to be pointed at us and kicked for the attack-denial clause, which is not targeted. This pass drops ruby storm and goryos vengeance and adds esper goryo, the same Goryo's Vengeance combo shell the card was already boarded for under the instant reanimator row.

deck_tech.name: Abiding Grace returns Martyr of Sands every end step
deck_tech.quirk: Nine life a turn off one enchantment, and the number that turns every Serra Ascendant into a 6/6 flier.
loop: Martyr of Sands is in the graveyard and Abiding Grace is on the battlefield
at our end step Abiding Grace returns it: Martyr is mana value one
pay one, reveal three white cards, sacrifice Martyr for nine life
Martyr is back in the graveyard in time for the next end step

lines.why: Nine a turn outruns any fair clock, and thirty life makes every Ascendant a 6/6 flier. It needs three white cards still in hand each turn to keep paying.

lines.mode: return Kami of False Hope instead
lines.why: One fog returned every end step answers a combo kill. Abiding Grace chooses one mode a turn, so it is the fog or the life and never both.

deck_tech.name: Evoking Solitude costs Martyr its count
deck_tech.quirk: Evoke exiles a white card from hand, and that is a card Martyr of Sands was going to reveal for three life.

lines.why: A turn-two Archon or a resolved combo creature ends the game before any amount of life matters. The exiled card costs three life we were never going to get to spend.
Nothing here kills us before turn five, so the hand keeps its white cards and Martyr keeps its count. Hard-cast it is also a lifelinking body that blocks.
Conqueror turns off Martyr, Kami of False Hope and the Clue. It is a 3/3 with no protection, and Solitude's exile is an enters trigger it does not touch.

deck_tech.name: White Orchid Phantom blinked for a land a turn
deck_tech.quirk: Land destruction that repeats, against the decks whose mana is their deck.
loop: resolve White Orchid Phantom and destroy one of their nonbasic lands
attack with Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd and exile the Phantom
at the next end step the Phantom returns and destroys a second land
attack again the following turn and repeat

lines.why: One nonbasic a turn against a deck that needs three specific ones. Ephemerate is the second engine: rebound makes one card two blinks across two turns.

deck_tech.name: The Serra clock, or the recursion grind
deck_tech.quirk: Which half of the deck this hand is: the fastest draw the deck has, or a game we win on cards.

lines.why: Turn-one Ascendant, turn-two Martyr revealing four white cards for twelve, then attack for six. Nothing else the deck does is this fast.
Emeria returns any creature at seven Plains and fifteen of the twenty-two lands carry the type. Against a deck answering one threat a turn we win on cards.

meta_calls.why: The Phantom's land kill comes back every turn off Phelia and Ephemerate, which is the angle a deck answering one threat at a time cannot keep pace with.
meta_calls.cost: One fewer permanent graveyard lock against Reanimator and the rest of the graveyard half of the field.

meta_calls.why: Their kill is three spells in one turn. High Noon allows one, so Summoner's Pact and the Titan cannot both happen and the Amulet turn stops being lethal.
meta_calls.cost: One fewer answer to Allosaurus, which the Chant was the board's whole plan against; ruby storm, its other target, left the field this pass.

meta_calls.why: It returns a Martyr or an Ascendant each upkeep out of the yard the sweeper just filled, costing them more energy to answer than the one-drops it rebuys.
meta_calls.cost: One fewer Solitude and Phantom rebuy, so the combo matchups lose a turn of tempo they were relying on.

gaps.why: The Rider is free but Neoform is {G}{U} and Eldritch Evolution {1}{G}{G}, so the kill is turn two off two lands - which means Orim's Chant is castable on both the play and the draw, and the problem is not the timing. It is that the Chant is the whole plan and Pact of Negation counters it for free on the turn it matters: three maindeck in ten of ten lists, and a fourth from the board in six of ten. Behind those, a resolved High Noon is destroyed by two Nature's Claim, which is maindeck in six of ten lists and boarded in eight, by two Natural State in the two boards that play it instead, and by a maindeck Boseiju, Who Endures channelled from hand in nine of ten; an Into the Flood Maw in ten of ten boards bounces it with the gift promised, and a Spell Snare in one board of ten answers it on the stack rather than after it resolves. Their four maindeck Consign to Memory do not belong in the count of answers to the tax: it counters a triggered ability or a colourless spell, and both Orim's Chant and High Noon are white. That does not make it a dead card here - post-board it answers the Phelia, Flickerwisp, Solitude, Skyclave Apparition, Starfield Shepherd and Overlord of the Balemurk triggers, which is most of the rest of our 60. The Abiding Grace end step is not one of them, because this row boards both copies out. Martyr of Sands is the exception on either count, since its ability is activated rather than triggered and is not a spell. On the draw only the one-mana half of our tax is deployed in time.
